LESSON: MINING IN KENYA

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Resources and Economic Activities
Topic 3.2: Mining in Kenya

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Mining in Kenya. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we benefit from the minerals found in our country?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify major minerals found in Kenya
2. use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MINING IN KENYA
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Mining in Kenya helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: MINING IN KENYA
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify major minerals found in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify major minerals found in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify major minerals found in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Mining in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify major minerals found in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals

What this means
In this part you learn to use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Mining in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Mining in Kenya is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Mining in Kenya” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify major minerals found in Kenya)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Mining in Kenya. (skill: use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Mining in Kenya to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify major minerals found in Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Mining in Kenya from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Mining in Kenya: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Mining in Kenya?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we benefit from the minerals found in our country?
2. How does the government promote mining in Kenya?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Mining in Kenya means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify major minerals found in Kenya.
5. Be able to: use the map of Kenya to locate major minerals.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
